title: Thus Saith the Lord, "the Spacious Fields
description: Thus Saith the Lord, "the Spacious Fields in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 50, part 2, headed “Second Part. C. M. Obedience is better than sacrifice”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thus saith the Lord, "the spa-cious fields "And flocks and herds are mine "O'er all the cat-tle of the hills "I claim a right di-vine.

lines: Thus saith the Lord, "the spacious fields
"O'er all the cattle of the hills
"To hope and love, to pray and praise,
"And those that tread my holy ways

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
